title: DP III: Knapsack Variants & Subsequence (LCS, Edit Distance, Subset-Sum, Partition)
relevance: 0/1 / unbounded knapsack, subset-sum, partition, LCS, and edit distance are among the most reused OA / interview DP patterns
company_notes: OA/interview flavors: budget/resource selection as 0/1 knapsack; equal-split/fair-division as partition/subset-sum (sometimes with remove-one or min-difference twists); change-making as min coins or number of ways (loop-order is a common reject); string transform/alignment as edit distance, LCS, or distinct-subsequence counting on disguised product/DNA strings.

phases.goal: Confirm the candidate maps wording to knapsack/subset-sum/partition vs two-string subsequence DP.

must_hit.point: “Maximum value under a budget” / pick items or projects under a cost cap maps to 0/1 knapsack.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names 0/1 knapsack or Book Shop / Knapsack 1 style maximize-under-cap.

must_hit.point: “Can you make sum / split equally” maps to subset-sum or partition (reduce to subset sum of total/2).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says partition equal subset sum or subset-sum reachability of half the total.

must_hit.point: “Longest common …” or “minimum operations to transform” maps to LCS or edit distance on two string prefixes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions LCS length/alignment or Levenshtein insert/delete/replace.

probes: What DP family is this—knapsack/subset-sum, or two-string subsequence—and what phrase in the prompt tipped you off?

hints.1: Look for a capacity/budget versus two sequences you must align or transform.
hints.2: Budget/max score → knapsack; equal split → subset-sum/partition; longest common / min edits → LCS or edit distance.
hints.3: Spot it when you see “maximum value under a budget”, “can you make sum / split equally”, “longest common …”, or “minimum operations to transform”.

phases.goal: Establish update direction, problem reductions, and the two-string transitions.

must_hit.point: 0/1 knapsack updates the 1D DP backward so each item is used at most once; unbounded updates forward.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States descending/backward for 0/1 and ascending/forward for unbounded/coin DP.

must_hit.point: Partition / Target Sum style problems reduce to “does a subset sum to T?” (or count such subsets), e.g. total/2 or (sum+target)/2.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly reduces fair split or signed-sum counting to a subset-sum instance.

must_hit.point: When capacity W is huge but values are small, flip state: dp[value] = min weight (Knapsack 2 pattern).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Swaps dimension to minimize weight for each value instead of indexing by weight.

must_hit.point: Subsequence string DP on prefixes: match/skip for LCS; insert/delete/replace for edit distance.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes dp[i][j] over two prefixes with those transition families.

probes: For this problem, is the inner update 0/1 or unbounded—and if it’s partition or Target Sum, what subset-sum target do you reduce to?

hints.1: Ask whether each item may be taken once or many times, and whether the ask is reachability, best value, or ways.
hints.2: Backward 1D for 0/1; forward for unbounded; partition/Target Sum → subset sum to total/2 or (sum+target)/2.
hints.3: If W is huge, use dp[value] = min weight; for two strings, LCS is match/skip and edit distance is insert/delete/replace.

phases.goal: Verify they can code 1D knapsack update order and the standard LCS / edit-distance transitions.

must_hit.point: Code 0/1 knapsack in O(nW) with a 1D array updated descending so each item is used at most once.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches nested loops with weight walking high→low for each item.

must_hit.point: Code unbounded / coin DP ascending; know outer-capacity vs outer-coin loop order distinguishes permutations vs combinations.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions ascending updates and that Coin Combinations I vs II differ by loop order.

must_hit.point: Edit distance: on match dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]; else 1 + min(insert, delete, replace).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the three mismatch transitions plus the equal-char copy.

must_hit.point: Optional stretch: bitset reachability via dp |= dp << w when only yes/no subset-sum matters.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions shifting/OR bitset trick for achievable sums.

probes: Walk through the 1D update for one item, then write the edit-distance recurrence for dp[i][j].

hints.1: Think about whether reusing the same item in the same pass would be legal.
hints.2: 0/1: descend weights; unbounded: ascend; coins: loop order = combinations vs permutations.
hints.3: Match → dp[i-1][j-1]; else 1 + min(insert, delete, replace); subset-sum-only can use dp |= dp << w.

phases.goal: Anchor the classical 0/1 knapsack cost and when to change the state dimension.

must_hit.point: Classical 0/1 knapsack is O(nW) time with a 1D capacity array.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(nW) for the standard weight-indexed DP.

must_hit.point: If W is huge and values are small, switch to value-indexed state (min weight per value) instead of weight-indexed DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains flipping the dimension as in AtCoder Knapsack 2 rather than forcing large W.

probes: What is the time complexity of the standard 0/1 knapsack DP, and when do you refuse to index by W?

hints.1: Count states by items times capacities you actually store.
hints.2: Weight-indexed 0/1 is O(nW); huge W forces another state choice.
hints.3: Quote O(nW) for classical 0/1; if W is huge, use dp[value] = min weight.

phases.goal: Surface the reject-level bugs around loop order, update direction, and reductions.

must_hit.point: Coin “number of ways” problems: wrong loop order swaps combinations and permutations—a common OA reject.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out Coin Combinations I vs II / order-matters vs combinations loop-order bug.

must_hit.point: Updating ascending on a 0/1 item (or descending on unbounded) silently allows the wrong reuse pattern.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties direction of the 1D pass to at-most-once vs unlimited reuse.

must_hit.point: Counting partition ways (e.g. Two Sets II) needs modular arithmetic—answers are mod 10^9+7.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions taking ways modulo 10^9+7 for equal-sum splits of 1..n.

probes: What silent bug makes “ways to make amount” fail tests even when min-coins is correct?

hints.1: Compare your coin loops to whether order of coins should matter.
hints.2: Outer capacity / inner coin vs the twin order; also check 0/1 vs unbounded pass direction.
hints.3: Wrong loop order ↔ combinations vs permutations; wrong 1D direction ↔ illegal reuse; counting splits often mod 10^9+7.

tradeoffs.topic: 0/1 backward update vs unbounded forward update
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Descend the 1D capacity array for 0/1 so each item is used at most once; ascend for unbounded/coin DP so an item can be reused in the same pass.
Outer capacity / inner coin vs its twin decides whether order matters (permutations) or only combinations are counted—the CSES Coin Combinations I/II pair.
When W is huge but values are small, store min weight per value (Knapsack 2) instead of best value per weight.

tradeoffs.topic: Full subset-sum DP vs bitset reachability
tradeoffs.strong_answer: If only yes/no achievable sums matter, bitset dp |= dp << w is a fast reachability trick; use full DP when you need values, counts, or reconstruction.
Length is the base dp[i][j] table; recovering an actual LCS string needs parent backtracking (AtCoder LCS), not only the length.

gotchas.trap: Using the same ascending coin DP for both “order matters” and “combinations only”.
gotchas.correction: Treat loop order as part of the spec—Coin Combinations I vs II are twins; mismatch is a common reject.

gotchas.trap: Updating 0/1 knapsack forward in 1D (or unbounded backward).
gotchas.correction: 0/1 must update descending so each item is used at most once; unbounded must update ascending.

gotchas.trap: Trying to solve equal-split / Target Sum without a subset-sum reduction.
gotchas.correction: Reduce to “subset sums to T” (or count such subsets), e.g. total/2 or (sum+target)/2.

gotchas.trap: Implementing only LCS length when the judge wants the string.
gotchas.correction: Keep parents / backtrack to reconstruct one LCS, as in AtCoder Educational DP F.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting modular reduction on partition counting.
gotchas.correction: Ways to split into equal sums (Two Sets II) are taken mod 10^9+7.
